nodes.summary: The loss of acting greedily on an approximate optimal value (Singh and Yee 1994; cf. AJKS Lemma 1.11), and its consequence for value iteration. Stated for deterministic greedy policies, with the API of value iteration.
nodes.title: Greedy policies of approximate values

nodes.summary: The linear quadratic regulator (LQR) controls the linear system $x_{t+1} = A x_t + B u_t$ so as to minimize the quadratic cost $\sum_t (x_t^\top Q x_t + u_t^\top R u_t)$. Recht (2019) uses it as the baseline on which to compare reinforcement learning methods: with known dynamics, dynamic programming solves it exactly. The cost-to-go is a quadratic form $x^\top M_t x$, the optimal control is the linear state…
nodes.title: Linear quadratic regulator

nodes.summary: Softmax policies and the natural policy gradient iteration, which for softmax policies is multiplicative weights on the advantages in every state, with its improvement lower bound and its dimension-free global convergence rate (Agarwal, Kakade, Lee and Mahajan 2021, Section 5.3).
nodes.title: Natural policy gradient

nodes.summary: Action values, advantages and discounted state occupancies of stochastic policies; the performance difference lemma of Kakade and Langford and its corollaries: policy improvement for stochastic policies and the improvement guarantee of conservative policy iteration.
nodes.title: Performance difference lemma

nodes.summary: Wanted results: the policy gradient theorem for softmax policies and the asymptotic global convergence of softmax policy gradient ascent (Agarwal, Kakade, Lee and Mahajan 2021, Section 5.1). Their proofs are deferred.
nodes.title: Policy gradients for softmax policies

nodes.summary: The value gap between two models with the same rewards, for a fixed stochastic policy, and the resulting value accuracy of an accurate model (AJKS Chapter 2). This is the deterministic core of model-based sample-complexity bounds with a generative model.
nodes.title: Simulation lemma

nodes.summary: Stationary stochastic policies on finite discounted Markov decision processes, Markov reward processes and their values, and discounted state visitation (AJKS Chapter 1). A deterministic policy embeds as a Dirac policy with the same value, so this layer extends value and policy iteration.
nodes.title: Stochastic policies and discounted occupancy

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
